breakthrough.rationale: JUDGED. Up: AP wire plus 52 outlets in one day; four newsletters led with it and Axios AM/Playbook PM ran it second; national TV (CNN AC360 interview, Fox, PBS, Cruz on The View); 100M+ reported views; 24–26 members of Congress within 24h including the Senate Commerce chair; 21 caucus members = 11.3% of the members who posted on 9/9; a live X rate of 18.33 posts/min at 3 AM ET two nights later; 19.4% non-English relay; parody copypasta and a memecoin, which signal saturation. Down: it was not the Beltway lead — Politico Playbook AM and Punchbowl AM 9/9 ignored it and the Dallas convention led most tip sheets; Jeffries, Johnson and Thune are all silent; no White House response; no Anthropic statement; tech ranked only 8 of 15 macros in the caucus's own day; no second-day decay or growth has been measured (recent-search pages cannot measure volume). Score would rise past 85 if leadership or the White House engages or a hearing is scheduled; it would fall below 60 if the 9/10 rate is measured well under the 9/8–9/9 originals-only rates (2.68 and 1.59/min) and no member posts on 9/10.

judged.caucusPosture: JUDGED. Fast (first original 07:01 ET, one minute behind a Republican), broad (21 members across Progressive 15, New Dem 10, CAPAC 4, CHC 5, CBC 1) and top-heavy (Lieu + Casar = 53% of originals' engagement; 9 of 23 originals under 200 likes). It is an emergency-plus-remedy posture with no shared remedy: nine different asks (Casar/Sanders ban; Lieu/Moran Kill Switch; Trahan/Obernolte FRONTIER; Khanna federal agency + 5 points; Gallego Senate select committee; Morrison cancel recess; Foster physical containment; García ban + data-center pause; Ryan emergency hearings), none echoed by a second member. The only shared language is a phrase ('the call is coming from inside the house' — Trahan, Morrison) and a rhythm ('pump the brakes' / 'heads in the sand' — Deluzio, Balint). The hearings/oversight ask is the remedy most members converge on (Casar, Ryan, Morrison, McClellan, Ramirez, Gallego, Khanna, Lieu's RT of Politico) and the one the Beltway press is already running (Politico Pro select-committee scoop; Washington Sun/Igor Bobic on Robert Garcia). Leadership is present only as Lieu/Trahan (leadership-tagged members posting their own bills) and as Jeffries briefed and having 'expressed openness' in Politico Pro — no Leader-level line exists. The intra-Democratic ban-vs-guardrails split (Sanders/Casar/Jayapal/Ansari/García vs Gottheimer/Trahan/Lieu/Beyer/Liccardo) was framed by Politico Pro within 24h. The surveillance/pre-crime angle the owner flagged reached the caucus once (Castro RT) and did not spread.

gopCounterMessage.what: JUDGED, two layers. (1) Elected Republicans did not rebut; they co-signed with a China condition and a no-ban condition: Cruz on The View 'highly concerning... I'd rather they be American killer robots than Chinese killer robots' (Politico Pro; TMZ; @SenTedCruz 2097727324011536877); Luna first member to post, special session (@RepLuna 2097641199196684682); Moran 'a priority in the next Congress' (Politico Pro; his X post 'innovation and safety are not mutually exclusive' is tracker-only, UNVERIFIED); Lawler 'broad consensus... they want a regulatory framework'; Chip Roy 'can't just go in and say government's got the solution — they're just going to ban it all... some friggin' leadership'; DeSantis/Uthmeier 'Frankenstein'. Johnson and Thune spokespeople silent; no markup; Senate Commerce has no AI hearings scheduled for four months. (2) The administration's operative line predates the thread: Bessent 9/8 'We can't pause... the Chinese won't pause. Even the North Koreans' (Breitbart); no White House statement on Coxon; Politico's Mak: WH 'really does not like Anthropic... woke'. (3) The real counter-message is in online-right/tech-right accounts and it is the most-engaged post in the sample: 'six weeks at Anthropic, socials appeared yesterday, coordinated op through doomer mega donors and the corporate media' (@JordanSchachtel 14,518 likes) and 'reposted by AI-safetyist foundations tied to Dustin Moskowitz... Ro Khanna' (@AFpost), plus 'regulatory capture / IPO marketing' and 'China wins if we pause'. The Sacks 'regulatory capture... fear-mongering' quote in circulation is from 2025-10-14, not this week (coverage.json claim, snowflake-dated).

risksForDems: Fragmented remedy menu: nine asks, no bill echoed twice; Politico Forecast already quotes Brugger that House Dems are 'talking a big game' — an easy 'they can't agree on what to do' line for the other side (caucus.json judged.shape[3]; coverage.json Forecast row).

The intra-Democratic ban-vs-guardrails split is on the record within 24h (Gottheimer on Sanders: 'not living in reality'; Jayapal 'push out the executives' vs Beyer 'bills are being written') and Politico Pro has framed it (coverage.json measured_vs_judged.judged[1]).

Messenger risk: the most-engaged post in the sample attacks Coxon's biography ('six weeks', 'socials appeared yesterday') and ties the Democratic response to a donor operation naming Khanna; the WSJ pre-arrangement is timing-supported (13-minute gap) and Coxon's tenure is inconsistent across sources (IBTimes 'OpenAI until July 2026' vs Axios 'four months at Anthropic' vs Schachtel 'six weeks'). 13 of 34 caucus posts quote Coxon's post directly and one retweets it (14 references, caucus.json sourcesReferenced).

Anthropic proximity: 'Presented by Anthropic' on Playbook AM/PM and Axios AM this week, Amodei as a Public First PAC donor, and Anthropic's own pro-restriction moves (quit ITI over China-chip bills) let the 'regulatory capture' frame attach to any Democrat carrying the company's safety line (coverage.json anthropic_response.same_cycle_corporate_actions).
China framing: every pause/ban ask draws 'unilateral disarmament' (replies to Casar in the sample; Bessent 9/8; Cruz 'American killer robots'); the ban camp is most exposed.

The Prospect 'pre-crime' story is a separate Anthropic-negative thread with progressive uptake (Castro RT; 70 of 276 sampled RTs are its two originals) that can tangle 'regulate frontier AI' with 'Anthropic surveils activists' inside the coalition (caucus.json judged.shape[6]).

Public salience may be thinner than the volume suggests: Third Way poll via Politico CA Decoded — only 35% 'very concerned' about AI's pace (reported, not read here); parody copypasta in the sample signals fatigue as much as reach.
The office's own pipeline was blind: 28 of 34 caucus posts filed as bare 'tech', no story candidate, no report line, and no 9/9 posts captured until ~01:30 ET 9/10 (caucus.json problems[0..5]).
opportunitiesForDems: A hearings/oversight ask is the one remedy most members already share and Republicans have co-signed in principle (Luna special session; Cruz 'highly concerning'; Lawler 'broad consensus'); Republican leadership's silence and 'no AI hearings for four months' is a measured contrast (coverage.json political_responses).

The select-committee track already has leadership traction (Jeffries briefed and 'expressed openness'; Lieu/Foster leading; Gallego's Senate letter; Robert Garcia's Oversight pledge) and is the frame Politico Pro and Washington Sun are running — the Beltway press is asking 'will Congress act?', which is the caucus's question.

Two bipartisan bills are already in members' mouths (Lieu/Moran AI Kill Switch — the largest caucus post at 8,007 likes; Trahan/Obernolte FRONTIER) — a 'name the bipartisan bill Johnson won't schedule' line does not require settling ban-vs-guardrails.

The company's own people, still employed, endorsed the number (Hubinger >10%, Marks 'the more senior the employee, the more concerned') and both labs disclosed summer breakouts — arguments that do not depend on Coxon's biography.

The story has crossed to general-audience and non-English audiences (AC360, Fox, PBS, Univision's @fdbedout 3,450 likes; 19.4% non-English in the sample), and shared language exists ('the call is coming from inside the house').
whatToWatchNext: Whether Jeffries or the Leader's office takes a position (select committee, hearings) — Politico Pro has him briefed and having 'expressed openness', with spokespeople not responding to requests for comment.

Whether the 'coordinated op / Khanna' line moves from @JordanSchachtel/@AFpost to an elected Republican or the White House — a genuine Sacks post about Coxon would be the tell (none as of 07:00Z 9/10; the circulating quote is from 2025).
Any Anthropic statement, and whether mainstream outlets merge the Prospect surveillance story with the resignation (not merged as of 9/10 07Z).

Congress's return next week (Khanna: 'when members return to Washington next week'): hearing requests, the Sanders/Casar bill's actual introduction, Cruz's catastrophic-risk bill with Thune-Klobuchar, Lieu/Foster select-committee planning.

Whether Republican engagement stays China-conditioned or produces legislation; whether Playbook AM/Punchbowl AM pick it up on 9/10.
